questions.q: What gap does Chapter 5's automation close that still existed after Chapters 2-4?
options: The database was still unprovisioned
The database was still unsecured
Health checks, backup verification, and alerting still depended on someone manually running and remembering to run them
The failover group had never been tested
questions.explain: Chapters 2-4 provisioned, secured, and protected the database, but kept depending on manual effort — exactly what this chapter's automation removes.

questions.q: Why does this lesson use dbatools instead of just clicking through SSMS for automation?
options: SSMS cannot connect to Azure SQL at all
SSMS is a GUI built for a human clicking through menus one server at a time — dbatools is purpose-built for the repetitive, unattended automation work a GUI can't do
dbatools is required by Microsoft for Azure SQL
SSMS doesn't support T-SQL
questions.explain: dbatools fills the gap SSMS was never designed for: scheduled, unattended, repeatable administration work.

options: Plain text output that must be parsed manually
Real PowerShell objects, immediately usable with Where-Object or foreach
An error unless run interactively in SSMS
A CSV file written to disk
questions.explain: Because the output is a real object collection, it plugs directly into ordinary PowerShell filtering and iteration.

questions.q: Why does the Invoke-DbaQuery example in this lesson connect to `overlook-fg.database.windows.net` rather than `overlook-sql-prod` directly?
options: Because overlook-sql-prod no longer exists
Because that's Chapter 4's failover group listener endpoint — connecting to it means the script keeps working no matter which region is currently primary, instead of breaking after a failover
Because dbatools cannot connect to named servers
There is no real reason; either would work identically
questions.explain: A script hardcoded to a specific server name would break after a failover — the listener endpoint is the correct, failover-safe target.

options: A paid Microsoft product bundled with SQL Server licenses
A free, open-source PowerShell module maintained by the SQL Server community, purpose-built for SQL Server administration
A built-in feature of Azure SQL requiring no installation
A replacement for the Azure Portal
questions.explain: dbatools installs the same way the Az module does — a free, community-maintained PowerShell module.
